title: Martha
summary: Martha appears in the Gospel narratives and helps frame Jesus' identity, mission, or response to his ministry.
historical_context: The setting is first-century Jewish life under Roman rule, especially in Galilee and Judea.
ancient_near_east_context: Household life, synagogue life, pilgrimage, and Roman administration form the social backdrop.
literary_context: The Gospels use Martha to show how people encounter Jesus and respond to his kingdom proclamation.
covenantal_significance: Martha sits within the movement from promise to fulfillment in Christ.
interpretive_notes: Read Gospel figures within the narrative, not just as isolated character sketches.
The Gospels use these figures to reveal something about Jesus and the kingdom.
common_questions: Why does this figure matter in the Gospels?
How does this figure respond to Jesus?
